entries.title: ask no attestation of 0.21.0, and drop unpublished pins from the lockfile
entries.body:
install.sh, and so scripts/fetch-seed.sh, verified a build provenance attestation for every release after 0.20.0. The attestation step (#898) landed after v0.21.0 was tagged, so 0.21.0 carries none, and every `binaries` row of the v0.22.0 release refused its 0.21.0 seed. Nothing was published, so the release's `lockfile` job never ran, and main's lockfile kept its platform packages at 0.21.0 against package.json's 0.22.0, which turned ci.yml's `npm ls --package-lock-only` red.

The threshold is now "after 0.21.0". The lockfile is regenerated with `npm install --package-lock-only`, which omits the four platform packages while 0.22.0 is not on the registry; the next release's `lockfile` job writes them back.
tests: tests/fetch-seed.js "install.sh asks for no attestation from 0.21.0
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: coalesce the Conduit server's same-shape reads into one array-parameter statement
entries.body:
Each Conduit worker now answers the waiting reads of one shape with a single
Postgres execution. Article and comment reads run as one statement over
unnest($1::text[], $2::int8[]) WITH ORDINALITY, with each request's viewer
bound per element, and rows routed back by ordinal. A missing slug answers
404 for its own request only. The parameterless tags read answers every
request that was waiting before it was sent, and no result outlives that
execution. Writes are unchanged and still commit before their response.

The read pool gets its own maxInFlight (DB_READ_IN_FLIGHT=4) so PgPool opens
more than one read connection while coalescing keeps the queue short. The
notebook records O9 to O11, kept and not, and the projection. A concurrency
check fails if any concurrent read differs from its serial answer or if
nothing was coalesced.

CI: every Ubuntu LLVM install moves off the Azure apt mirror, and the
installs that lacked one now share a cached, stall-cutting composite action
(.github/actions/apt-install).
metrics: Postgres -20.7 µs/request (-7.3%) paired against main at 4,000 users, think-scale 0.1, three pairs each outside the spread; p99 mean 201 against 173 ms
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon
